grain: One retail customer's ONE facility at ONE month-end.
rate_convention: Annual rates and ratios stored as decimals, not percentages.

columns.name: snapshot_date
columns.definition: The month-end this row describes. A row is the state of one facility ON this date.

columns.name: reporting_month
columns.definition: `snapshot_date` as YYYY-MM. The dataset's partition key.

columns.name: dataset_version
columns.definition: Generator version, configuration version and seed, pinned at publication.

columns.name: record_id
columns.definition: snapshot_date and facility_id joined. Unique within a published dataset version.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.definition: Synthetic natural-person customer identifier. Not a national ID and not a real account.

columns.name: facility_id
columns.definition: Synthetic facility identifier, stable across every month the facility is live.

columns.name: application_id
columns.definition: The originating application. One per booked facility in this demo book.

columns.name: product_code
columns.definition: Retail product family. The stable machine code; `product_label` is what a user reads.

columns.name: product_label
columns.definition: The retail product this facility is: Credit Card, Personal Finance, Auto Finance or Home Finance. The dimension almost every question about this book is grouped by.

columns.name: product_subsegment
columns.definition: The variant within the product — a first home against a refinance, a new car against a used one, new lending against a top-up. Products behave differently inside these splits.

columns.name: portfolio_country
columns.definition: The country of the lending book. SA throughout.

columns.name: currency
columns.definition: The currency of the facility. Saudi riyal throughout this book, so every amount is comparable without conversion.

columns.name: customer_relationship_start_date
columns.definition: The month-end on which the customer's first relationship with the bank opened. Earlier than the origination date of any one facility.

columns.name: customer_tenure_months
columns.definition: Whole months since the customer's relationship with the bank began, measured to this month-end. A CUSTOMER attribute repeated on each of their facilities: averaging it across facility rows weights long relationships by how many products they hold.

columns.name: application_date
columns.definition: The month-end on which the customer applied.

columns.name: approval_date
columns.definition: The month-end on which the application was approved.

columns.name: origination_date
columns.definition: The month-end on which the facility was booked.

columns.name: origination_vintage
columns.definition: Origination month as YYYY-MM. The cohort key for vintage analysis.

columns.name: contractual_maturity_date
columns.definition: The month-end on which the last contractual payment falls due.

columns.name: original_tenor_months
columns.definition: The contractual term in months at origination.

columns.name: remaining_contractual_tenor_months
columns.definition: Months from this month-end to contractual maturity.

columns.name: months_on_book
columns.definition: Whole months from origination to this snapshot. Increases by exactly one per month.

columns.name: facility_status
columns.definition: Whether the facility is OPEN or CLOSED at this month-end. A closed facility keeps its row so the history can be read; it carries no exposure.

columns.name: closure_date
columns.definition: The month-end on which the facility closed, where it has.

columns.name: closure_reason
columns.definition: Why the facility closed: SETTLED_EARLY, MATURED or WRITTEN_OFF. The third is a credit loss and the first two are not.

columns.name: refinanced_from_facility_id
columns.definition: The facility this one refinanced, where it refinanced one. A chain of refinancings is a repayment difficulty that never showed as DPD.

columns.name: restructured_flag
columns.definition: Whether the facility's terms were restructured. Restructuring without financial difficulty is not forbearance; the two flags are separate for that reason.

columns.name: restructure_date
columns.definition: When the facility was restructured.

columns.name: source_system
columns.definition: Which system this row came from. A synthetic generator here, stated rather than implied.

columns.name: source_record_id
columns.definition: The key of the source record this row was built from, so any figure can be traced back to what the source system sent.

columns.name: source_available_at
columns.definition: When the source data became available. Read with `calculation_available_at` it says how long the book took to close.

columns.name: is_synthetic
columns.definition: Whether the row is synthetic. True on every row of this book: it is demonstration data, and this column is what makes that checkable rather than a claim in a footnote.

columns.name: generator_version
columns.definition: The version of the synthetic generator that produced this book.

columns.name: data_quality_status
columns.definition: Whether this row passed the publication quality checks. THIN_HISTORY marks a facility with too little history to score, which is a state rather than a fault.

columns.name: customer_scope
columns.definition: The population this book covers: natural persons borrowing for themselves. It is one value everywhere, and it is the sentence that says why no company appears in this dataset.

columns.name: score_subject_grain
columns.definition: What one scored row IS. FACILITY here: a customer with three facilities has three scores, and averaging them is not a customer score.

columns.name: region
columns.definition: The Saudi administrative region of the customer's address, as a code. `region_label` is the same thing written for a reader.

columns.name: region_label
columns.definition: The Saudi administrative region of the customer's address, written the way it is shown on screen.

columns.name: city
columns.definition: The city of the customer's registered address.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.definition: The branch that booked the facility.

columns.name: origination_channel
columns.definition: How the facility was sold: BRANCH, DIGITAL, PARTNER, DEALER or RELATIONSHIP_MANAGER. Channels differ in default rate at the same score, which is the point of measuring it.

columns.name: customer_segment
columns.definition: The bank's relationship segment — MASS, MASS_AFFLUENT, AFFLUENT or PRIVATE — set from income and holdings, not from credit quality.

columns.name: new_to_bank_at_origination_flag
columns.business_name: New to bank at origination flag
columns.definition: Whether the customer was new to the bank when this facility was booked. A new-to-bank customer is scored without internal history.

columns.name: residency_category
columns.definition: Whether the customer is a Saudi citizen or a resident. It changes which affordability and tenor rules a product applies.

columns.name: age_band
columns.definition: The customer's age at this month-end, in bands. Banded rather than exact so an age cannot identify a person in a demonstration book.

columns.name: dependants_band
columns.definition: How many dependants the customer declared at origination, in bands. An input to the household expense floor, not to the score.

columns.name: employment_status
columns.definition: Where the customer's income comes from: GOVERNMENT, GOVERNMENT_RELATED, PRIVATE_SECTOR, SELF_EMPLOYED or RETIRED. The strongest single non-behavioural predictor in this book.

columns.name: employer_id
columns.definition: The employer paying the salary, as a key. Concentration by employer is a retail risk in its own right where one employer pays many customers of the same book.

columns.name: employer_sector
columns.definition: The economic sector of the customer's employer. The retail book's nearest equivalent of an industry exposure: it says what a salary depends on, not what the borrower does.

columns.name: employment_tenure_months
columns.definition: Whole months in current employment at this month-end. A CUSTOMER attribute repeated on every facility they hold.

columns.name: salary_transfer_flag
columns.definition: Whether the customer's salary is transferred to this bank. The single most important affordability control in Saudi retail lending: it is what makes an instalment deductible at source.

columns.name: salary_verification_status
columns.definition: How income was evidenced: VERIFIED_TRANSFER, where the salary lands in an account at this bank, or DECLARED_DOCUMENTED, where it was documented but is paid elsewhere. The first is materially stronger.

columns.name: verified_monthly_salary_sar
columns.definition: Monthly salary the bank has verified, at this month-end. A CUSTOMER level: summing it across a customer's facilities counts one person's income several times over.

columns.name: verified_other_monthly_income_sar
columns.definition: Verified monthly income other than salary — rent, pension, a second trade. A CUSTOMER level, repeated on each facility.

columns.name: verified_total_monthly_income_sar
columns.definition: Verified monthly salary plus verified other income. A CUSTOMER property repeated on each of their facilities: summing it over facility rows counts one income several times.
columns.aggregation: one value per customer; never multiplied by facility count

columns.name: household_expenses_sar
columns.definition: The monthly household expense figure used in the affordability test at this month-end — the larger of what the customer declared and the policy floor for their dependants band.

columns.name: monthly_external_credit_obligations_sar
columns.definition: Monthly instalments owed to OTHER lenders, from the bureau. A CUSTOMER level, repeated on each facility.

columns.name: monthly_own_bank_credit_obligations_sar
columns.business_name: Monthly own bank credit obligations SAR
columns.definition: Monthly instalments owed to THIS bank across all of the customer's facilities, at this month-end. A CUSTOMER level.

columns.name: monthly_total_credit_obligations_sar
columns.definition: Own-bank obligations, including this facility's instalment exactly once, plus verified external obligations.

columns.name: obligation_scope_definition
columns.definition: Which obligations the debt burden ratio counts, stated so the denominator can be reproduced.

columns.name: disposable_income_sar
columns.definition: Verified income less household expenses less all credit obligations. Not salary, and not income: three different quantities kept in three different columns.

columns.name: debt_burden_ratio
columns.definition: monthly_total_credit_obligations_sar / verified_total_monthly_income_sar at this snapshot.

columns.name: affordability_buffer_sar
columns.definition: Verified income less household expenses and every monthly credit obligation. What is left each month once the household has paid what it must. Negative means the arithmetic does not close.

columns.name: income_band
columns.definition: Verified monthly income at this month-end, in bands. Banded for grouping; `verified_monthly_salary_sar` carries the figure.

columns.name: indebtedness_band
columns.definition: Total monthly credit obligations as a share of verified income, in bands — the debt burden ratio a reader groups by.

columns.name: policy_version_at_origination
columns.definition: The version of the credit policy — cutoffs and rules — in force when this facility was decided.

columns.name: policy_exception_flag
columns.definition: Whether the facility was booked outside policy — below cutoff, or past an affordability limit.

columns.name: policy_exception_reason
columns.definition: Which policy the exception was against, in words.

columns.name: score_override_flag
columns.definition: Whether a human changed the score the model produced.

columns.name: score_override_direction
columns.definition: Whether the override made the score better or worse.

columns.name: score_override_reason
columns.definition: Why the score was overridden, in words. An override rate and its reasons are a model governance finding in their own right.

columns.name: applied_score_cutoff
columns.definition: The application score cutoff that applied to this facility at origination. A facility booked below it is a policy exception.

columns.name: decision_at_origination
columns.definition: What the credit decision was. Every facility in a book of BOOKED facilities was approved; declined applications are not here, which is why an approval rate cannot be computed from this dataset.

columns.name: employment_change_flag
columns.definition: Whether the employer on record changed since the previous month-end. A change is not itself adverse; a change WITH a salary interruption is what the early warning rules read.

columns.name: job_loss_reported_flag
columns.definition: Whether a loss of employment has been reported for this customer. Declared or inferred — `job_loss_signal_source` says which.

columns.name: job_loss_signal_source
columns.definition: Where the job-loss signal came from. In this synthetic book it is a customer declaration; in a real installation it would name the channel that reported it.

columns.name: original_finance_amount_sar
columns.definition: The amount financed at origination. Fixed for the life of the facility; it does not move as the balance amortises.

columns.name: original_credit_limit_sar
columns.definition: The credit limit set at origination. On a card this is what the customer may draw; on an instalment facility it equals the amount financed.

columns.name: current_credit_limit_sar
columns.definition: Approved card limit in force at this month-end. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: outstanding_principal_sar
columns.definition: Principal outstanding at this month-end, before accrued profit. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: accrued_profit_interest_sar
columns.definition: Profit or interest accrued and unpaid at this month-end. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: undrawn_commitment_sar
columns.definition: Limit not drawn at this month-end. Card only. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: available_limit_sar
columns.definition: Limit still available to draw. Card only. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: scheduled_monthly_payment_sar
columns.definition: The instalment contractually due each month at this month-end.

columns.name: scheduled_payment_due_sar
columns.definition: Amount contractually due in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: actual_payment_received_sar
columns.definition: Amount actually received in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: principal_repayment_sar
columns.definition: Principal repaid in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: new_drawdown_sar
columns.definition: New amounts drawn in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: accrued_charges_sar
columns.definition: Profit or interest charged in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: capitalised_amount_sar
columns.definition: Amounts capitalised into the balance in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: writeoff_amount_month_sar
columns.definition: Amount written off in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: recovery_amount_month_sar
columns.definition: Amount recovered in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: other_balance_adjustment_sar
columns.definition: Any other movement in this month. A PERIOD amount: aggregate over the months of the period wanted.
columns.aggregation: sum across months in a period

columns.name: nominal_annual_profit_interest_rate
columns.definition: The contractual annual profit rate, as a decimal. Nominal: it does not include fees and is not what the customer effectively pays.

columns.name: rate_type
columns.definition: Whether the profit rate is FIXED for the term or FLOATING against a benchmark. Floating facilities carry instalment risk to the customer.

columns.name: contract_structure
columns.definition: The Islamic financing structure: MURABAHA (cost-plus sale), TAWARRUQ (monetisation) or IJARA (lease). It decides how profit is recognised, not how risk is measured.

columns.name: secured_flag
columns.definition: Whether the facility has collateral behind it. Home and auto facilities do; cards and personal finance do not.

columns.name: collateral_type
columns.definition: What secures the facility — RESIDENTIAL_PROPERTY or VEHICLE.

columns.name: collateral_value_origination_sar
columns.definition: The collateral's appraised value at origination. Not revalued: the current LTV moves with the balance, not with the property.

columns.name: collateral_value_current_sar
columns.definition: Latest valuation of the security held. Secured products only. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: collateral_valuation_date
columns.definition: When the collateral was last valued.

columns.name: vehicle_new_used
columns.definition: Whether the financed vehicle was new or used at origination.

columns.name: vehicle_age_months
columns.definition: The vehicle's age in months at this month-end.

columns.name: dealer_id
columns.definition: The dealer that introduced an auto facility. Dealer concentration and dealer-level default rates are an origination quality question.

columns.name: down_payment_sar
columns.definition: What the customer paid up front at origination.

columns.name: balloon_payment_sar
columns.definition: A final lump sum due at the end of the term, above the regular instalments. Zero where the facility fully amortises.

columns.name: balloon_due_date
columns.definition: When the balloon payment falls due.

columns.name: housing_support_flag
columns.definition: Whether the customer receives government housing support on this facility. It changes the instalment the household actually pays.

columns.name: housing_support_type
columns.definition: Which housing support programme applies, or NONE.

columns.name: property_type
columns.definition: What kind of property secures a home facility.

columns.name: home_purpose
columns.definition: Why the home facility was taken: FIRST_HOME, SECOND_PROPERTY or REFINANCE.

columns.name: auto_structure
columns.definition: The financing structure for a vehicle facility — MURABAHA or IJARA. Under IJARA the bank holds title until the final payment.

columns.name: previous_month_dpd
columns.definition: Days past due at the PREVIOUS month-end. Held on the row so a movement can be read without joining the book to itself.

columns.name: dpd_bucket
columns.definition: `dpd` banded. CURRENT means zero days past due.

columns.name: overdue_amount_sar
columns.definition: Amounts contractually due and unpaid at this month-end. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: oldest_unpaid_due_date
columns.definition: The due date of the oldest instalment still unpaid. It is what days past due is counted from.

columns.name: current_default_flag
columns.definition: In default at this month-end under the versioned default definition: 90+ DPD, or recorded unlikeliness to pay. A cured facility is False here and keeps its `first_default_date`.

columns.name: first_default_date
columns.definition: When this facility first defaulted.

columns.name: latest_default_date
columns.definition: When this facility most recently defaulted.

columns.name: default_reason
columns.definition: Which limb of the default definition was met.

columns.name: default_episode_id
columns.definition: The key of this default episode. A facility that defaults, cures and defaults again has two episodes, and counting defaults without this column counts the customer twice.

columns.name: credit_impaired_flag
columns.definition: Whether the facility is credit-impaired — Stage 3. Not the same as written off, and not the same as in collections.

columns.name: unlikeliness_to_pay_flag
columns.definition: Whether default was called on unlikeliness to pay rather than on days past due. It is what catches a default that never showed as arrears.

columns.name: forbearance_flag
columns.definition: Whether the facility has been granted forbearance — a concession made because the customer was in financial difficulty.

columns.name: forbearance_start_date
columns.definition: When forbearance was granted.

columns.name: cure_flag
columns.definition: Whether the facility has cured out of default.

columns.name: cure_date
columns.definition: When the facility cured.

columns.name: cure_probation_months
columns.definition: How many months a cured facility must stay current before it leaves default. A cure inside probation is not yet a cure.

columns.name: writeoff_flag
columns.definition: Whether the balance has been written off. A write-off removes the asset; it does not end the claim on the customer.

columns.name: cumulative_writeoff_sar
columns.definition: Total written off on this facility to date. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: collections_stage
columns.definition: How far into collections the facility has gone: NONE, SOFT_REMINDER, TELE_COLLECTION, FIELD, LEGAL or WRITE_OFF.

columns.name: contact_attempts_3m
columns.definition: Collections contact attempts in the last three months.

columns.name: promise_to_pay_flag
columns.definition: Whether the customer has an outstanding promise to pay.

columns.name: promise_to_pay_due_date
columns.definition: When the promised payment is due.

columns.name: days_30plus_count_12m
columns.definition: Days spent at 30 or more days past due over twelve months.

columns.name: months_30plus_count_12m
columns.definition: Month-ends at 30 or more days past due over twelve months. Three separate month-ends in arrears is a different risk from one long spell, and this is the column that tells them apart.

columns.name: full_payment_months_6m
columns.definition: Months in the last six in which the full instalment was paid.

columns.name: card_behaviour_segment
columns.definition: How the card is used: TRANSACTOR (settled in full), REVOLVER (carries a balance) or INACTIVE. The same limit is a different risk in each.

columns.name: utilisation_band
columns.definition: Current utilisation, in bands. Above 100% means an overlimit balance.

columns.name: ltv_band
columns.definition: The current loan-to-value ratio, in bands.

columns.name: down_payment_band
columns.definition: The down payment as a share of the asset price, in bands.

columns.name: balloon_band
columns.definition: The balloon as a share of the amount financed, in bands. NONE where there is no balloon.

columns.name: bureau_score_origination_date
columns.definition: When the origination bureau score was drawn.

columns.name: bureau_score_current_date
columns.definition: When the current bureau score was drawn.

columns.name: bureau_score_scale_id
columns.definition: The scale the bureau score is expressed on, so scores from different vintages are not compared across scales.

columns.name: bureau_active_facilities_count
columns.definition: Facilities the customer has open with other lenders.

columns.name: bureau_total_exposure_sar
columns.definition: Total balances owed to other lenders. A CUSTOMER level: summing it over a customer's facilities counts the same external debt twice.

columns.name: bureau_adverse_flag
columns.definition: Whether the bureau reports an adverse event — a default, a judgment or a write-off — with another lender.

columns.name: bureau_thin_file_flag
columns.definition: Whether the bureau holds too little history to score reliably. A thin file is not a bad file, and treating it as one is a known way to decline good customers.

columns.name: bureau_data_available_flag
columns.definition: Whether bureau data was returned at all for this customer.

columns.name: bureau_source_label
columns.definition: Which bureau the external data came from. Synthetic here: this book carries a bureau PROXY, not SIMAH data.

columns.name: bureau_data_freshness_days
columns.definition: How old the bureau data is, in days, at this month-end.

columns.name: salary_credit_last_date
columns.definition: The month-end of the most recent salary credit received.

columns.name: expected_salary_credit_date
columns.definition: When the next salary credit is due, from the customer's pattern.

columns.name: salary_delay_days
columns.definition: Days between when the salary was expected and when it arrived. Zero where it arrived on time.

columns.name: account_inflows_1m_sar
columns.definition: Everything credited to the customer's accounts in this month, salary included. A PERIOD amount: sum it over the months of the period wanted, never across a level.

columns.name: account_outflows_1m_sar
columns.definition: Everything debited from the customer's accounts in this month. A PERIOD amount.

columns.name: application_score_date
columns.definition: When the application score was produced.

columns.name: application_score_direction
columns.definition: Which way the scale runs. HIGHER_IS_SAFER throughout, stated explicitly because a validation test that assumes the other direction reports every Gini with its sign reversed.

columns.name: application_score_status
columns.definition: Whether an application score exists, and why not where it does not.

columns.name: application_score_reconciled_flag
columns.definition: Whether the stored score was reproduced exactly from the stored inputs, the frozen bins and the published coefficients. False is an implementation defect, not a model outcome.

columns.name: behavioural_score_date
columns.definition: When the behavioural score was produced — this month-end.

columns.name: behavioural_score_direction
columns.definition: Which way the scale runs. HIGHER_IS_SAFER.

columns.name: behavioural_score_status
columns.definition: Whether a behavioural score exists. NOT_SCORED_THIN_HISTORY where the facility has too few months to score — a state, not a zero.

columns.name: behavioural_score_reconciled_flag
columns.definition: Whether the stored behavioural score was reproduced exactly from stored inputs, frozen bins and published coefficients.

columns.name: score_implementation_check_status
columns.definition: Whether the stored score was reproduced from its stored inputs. PASS means the implementation agrees with the specification.

columns.name: score_evidence_ref
columns.definition: The key of the stored evidence for this score — inputs, bins, weights and the arithmetic. What makes the score auditable.

columns.name: calculation_run_id
columns.definition: The key of the calculation run that produced this row. Two rows with the same run id were produced by the same code and the same inputs.

columns.name: calculation_available_at
columns.definition: When the calculated figures became available.

columns.name: dpd
columns.definition: Days past due at this month-end, derived from the oldest unpaid due date.

columns.name: max_dpd_3m
columns.definition: The worst days past due reached in the last three months. A facility can be current today and have been 60 days down in May.

columns.name: max_dpd_6m
columns.definition: The worst days past due reached in the last six months.

columns.name: max_dpd_12m
columns.definition: The worst days past due reached in the last twelve months.

columns.name: missed_payment_count_3m
columns.definition: Scheduled payments not made in the last three months.

columns.name: missed_payment_count_6m
columns.definition: Scheduled payments not made in the last six months.

columns.name: payment_to_due_ratio_1m
columns.definition: What was paid over what was due, in this month. Below 1 is a part payment; a card customer paying the minimum sits well below it.

columns.name: payment_to_due_ratio_3m
columns.definition: What was paid over what was due, across three months.

columns.name: utilisation_ratio
columns.definition: Drawn balance over current credit limit. Card only; an amortising loan has no utilisation.
columns.null_policy: Null for every non-revolving product, with product applicability as the reason. Never zero.

columns.name: utilisation_avg_3m
columns.definition: Average drawn balance over credit limit across three months.

columns.name: utilisation_change_3m_pp
columns.definition: Change in utilisation over three months, in percentage points. Already a difference: do not difference it again.

columns.name: minimum_payment_only_months_3m
columns.definition: Months in the last three where only the minimum payment was made.

columns.name: overlimit_days_3m
columns.definition: Days spent above the credit limit in the last three months.

columns.name: cash_advance_share_3m
columns.definition: Cash advances as a share of card spend over three months. Cash advance on a card is expensive money and is read as a liquidity signal, not as spending.

columns.name: salary_credit_amount_1m_sar
columns.definition: The salary credited to the customer's account in this month.

columns.name: salary_credit_average_3m_sar
columns.definition: Average monthly salary credit over three months, to this month-end.

columns.name: salary_credit_average_6m_sar
columns.definition: Average monthly salary credit over six months, to this month-end.

columns.name: salary_change_3m_ratio
columns.definition: The latest salary credit over the average of the three before it. Below 1 means the salary has fallen.

columns.name: salary_missed_cycle_count_3m
columns.definition: Salary cycles with no credit at all in the last three months.

columns.name: income_volatility_6m
columns.definition: Coefficient of variation of the last six salary credits. High means the income arrives in uneven amounts, whatever its average.

columns.name: balance_buffer_months
columns.definition: How many months of the scheduled instalment the customer's average account balance would cover. A liquidity cushion, not a level.

columns.name: account_average_balance_3m_sar
columns.definition: Average current-account balance over three months, to this month-end. A CUSTOMER level.

columns.name: bureau_score_current
columns.definition: The customer's bureau score at this month-end. Higher is safer.

columns.name: bureau_score_change_3m
columns.definition: Change in the bureau score over three months. Already a difference.

columns.name: bureau_external_dpd_max
columns.definition: Worst days past due with any other lender. A customer current here and 90 days down elsewhere is the case this column exists for.

columns.name: external_obligations_change_3m_sar
columns.definition: Change in monthly obligations to other lenders over three months. Positive means the customer has taken on borrowing elsewhere — the earliest visible sign of stress this book carries.

columns.name: bureau_enquiries_3m
columns.definition: Credit enquiries recorded at the bureau in three months. A burst of enquiries is a customer looking for money.

columns.name: bureau_enquiries_6m
columns.definition: Credit enquiries recorded at the bureau in six months.

columns.name: broken_promise_count_3m
columns.definition: Promises to pay that were made and not kept, over three months. A broken promise is a stronger signal than a missed instalment: the customer engaged and still did not pay.

columns.definition: Which behavioural scorecard scored this facility. One per product.

columns.name: behavioural_score_change_3m
columns.definition: Change in the behavioural score over three months. Already a difference: do not difference it again. A large fall is the deterioration signal the early warning rules read first.

columns.definition: Model inputs absent at scoring, across both scorecards.

columns.name: score_input_stale_count

columns.name: returned_payment_count_3m
columns.definition: Direct debits returned unpaid in the last three months.

columns.name: stage_entry_date
columns.definition: When the facility entered its current stage. How long it has been in Stage 2 matters as much as that it is.

columns.name: calculation_input_hash
columns.definition: A hash of the inputs to the calculation. Two runs with the same hash and different outputs is a reproducibility defect.

columns.name: origination_income_sar
columns.definition: Verified monthly income AT ORIGINATION. Frozen: it is what was underwritten, and comparing it with income now is how income drift is measured.

columns.name: origination_salary_sar
columns.definition: Verified monthly salary at origination. Frozen.

columns.name: origination_household_expenses_sar
columns.definition: The household expense figure used in the affordability test at origination. Frozen.

columns.name: origination_external_obligations_sar
columns.definition: Monthly obligations to other lenders at origination. Frozen.

columns.name: origination_own_bank_obligations_sar
columns.definition: Monthly obligations to this bank at origination. Frozen.

columns.name: origination_total_obligations_sar
columns.definition: All monthly credit obligations at origination. Frozen.

columns.name: origination_debt_burden_ratio
columns.definition: Total monthly obligations over income at origination. The ratio the affordability limit was tested against.

columns.name: origination_disposable_income_sar
columns.definition: Income less expenses and obligations at origination — the affordability buffer as it was underwritten.

columns.name: origination_employment_tenure_months
columns.definition: Months in employment at origination. Frozen.

columns.name: origination_customer_tenure_months
columns.definition: Months of relationship with the bank at origination. Zero for a new-to-bank customer.

columns.name: origination_salary_transfer_status
columns.definition: Whether the salary was transferred to this bank AT ORIGINATION. Frozen: it does not follow the customer if the arrangement lapses.

columns.name: bureau_score_at_origination
columns.definition: The bureau score as at origination. Frozen: comparing it with the current score measures how the customer has moved since underwriting.

columns.name: origination_bureau_enquiries_3m
columns.definition: Bureau enquiries in the three months before origination — how hard the customer was shopping for credit when they applied.

columns.name: origination_bureau_external_dpd_max
columns.definition: Worst days past due with any other lender, at origination.

columns.name: origination_bureau_active_facilities
columns.definition: Facilities open with other lenders at origination.

columns.name: origination_amount_to_income_ratio
columns.definition: Amount financed over monthly income at origination — how many months of income was lent.

columns.name: origination_instalment_to_income_ratio
columns.definition: This facility's instalment over income at origination.

columns.name: ltv_origination_ratio
columns.definition: Amount financed over collateral value at origination. A RATIO: recompute it from summed amounts, never average it across rows.

columns.name: origination_balloon_ratio
columns.definition: The balloon over the amount financed, at origination.

columns.name: origination_income_stability_ratio
columns.definition: How steady the income was over the months before origination. Low means it varied.

columns.name: gross_carrying_amount_sar
columns.definition: Outstanding principal plus accrued profit. The exposure the loss allowance is measured against. A month-end LEVEL: summing it across months does not give a portfolio total.

columns.name: ifrs9_stage
columns.definition: IFRS 9 impairment stage under the versioned synthetic staging policy.

columns.name: previous_month_stage
columns.definition: The IFRS 9 stage at the previous month-end. Held on the row so a stage migration can be read without joining the book to itself.

columns.name: staging_policy_version
columns.definition: The version of the staging policy that produced this stage.

columns.name: sicr_flag
columns.definition: Whether a significant increase in credit risk has been identified — the test that moves a facility from Stage 1 to Stage 2.

columns.name: sicr_reason
columns.definition: Which test moved this facility, in words. The sentence a reviewer reads when they ask why a facility is in Stage 2.

columns.name: sicr_quantitative_flag
columns.definition: Whether the SICR test was met on the quantitative limb: lifetime PD has risen enough against origination.

columns.name: sicr_qualitative_flag
columns.definition: Whether the SICR test was met on the qualitative limb — forbearance, repeated arrears, a behavioural collapse.

columns.name: sicr_dpd_backstop_flag
columns.definition: Whether the 30-days-past-due backstop alone moved this facility to Stage 2. A backstop-only population is one whose models saw nothing.

columns.name: stage_override_flag
columns.definition: Whether the stage was set by judgment rather than by the rules.

columns.name: stage_override_reason
columns.definition: Why the stage was overridden, in words.

columns.name: default_definition_id
columns.definition: The governed definition of default in force — 90 days past due or unlikeliness to pay.

columns.name: credit_risk_model_id
columns.definition: The IFRS 9 model set that produced the staging, PD, LGD and EAD on this row.

columns.name: pd_model_version
columns.definition: The version of the PD model.

columns.name: lgd_model_version
columns.definition: The version of the LGD model.

columns.name: ead_model_version
columns.definition: The version of the EAD model.

columns.name: ecl_model_version
columns.definition: The version of the ECL engine that produced the allowance.

columns.name: ifrs9_pd_source_model
columns.definition: Which scorecard the IFRS 9 PD was mapped from — the behavioural model where the facility has history, the application model where it does not.

columns.name: ifrs9_pd_mapping_version
columns.definition: The version of the score-to-PD mapping used.

columns.name: pd_ttc_12m
columns.definition: Through-the-cycle 12-month default probability. NOT the application or behavioural model's PD, and not the point-in-time PD: the mapping between them is versioned.

columns.name: pd_pit_12m_anchor
columns.definition: The twelve-month point-in-time PD before scenario weighting — the anchor the three scenarios are built around. A probability: never sum it, and recompute it over a population weighted by exposure.

columns.name: monthly_discount_rate
columns.definition: The effective annual rate converted to one month, which is the rate the ECL cashflows are actually discounted at.

columns.name: ecl_remaining_life_months
columns.definition: Months of expected life remaining at this month-end.

columns.name: ecl_contractual_remaining_months
columns.definition: Months to contractual maturity. Where this and the expected life differ, the behavioural assumption is doing the work.

columns.name: ecl_undrawn_commitment_sar
columns.definition: The undrawn limit the credit conversion factor was applied to.

columns.name: ecl_drawn_balance_sar
columns.definition: The drawn balance the ECL calculation started from.

columns.name: pd_ttc_at_origination_12m
columns.definition: The twelve-month through-the-cycle PD at origination — the same risk without the point in the cycle.

columns.name: pd_pit_at_origination_12m
columns.definition: The twelve-month point-in-time PD as at origination. Frozen: it is the denominator of the quantitative SICR test.

columns.name: pd_origination_curve_remaining_life
columns.definition: The origination PD curve read at the facility's remaining life, so the SICR comparison is like for like rather than comparing a remaining-life PD with a whole-life one.

columns.name: sicr_pd_ratio
columns.definition: Lifetime PD now over lifetime PD at origination. The quantitative SICR test compares this with its threshold.

columns.name: sicr_pd_absolute_change
columns.definition: Lifetime PD now minus lifetime PD at origination, in absolute terms. The second half of the quantitative test: a small PD can triple without becoming material.

columns.name: pd_pit_12m_base
columns.definition: Point-in-time 12-month default probability under the base scenario.

columns.name: pd_pit_12m_upturn
columns.definition: Twelve-month point-in-time PD under the upturn scenario.

columns.name: pd_pit_12m_downturn
columns.definition: Twelve-month point-in-time PD under the downturn scenario.

columns.name: pd_pit_lifetime_base
columns.definition: Cumulative default probability over the applicable remaining life, base scenario. A different quantity from the 12-month PD, not a rescaling of it.

columns.name: pd_pit_lifetime_upturn
columns.definition: Lifetime point-in-time PD under the upturn scenario.

columns.name: pd_pit_lifetime_downturn
columns.definition: Lifetime point-in-time PD under the downturn scenario.

columns.name: lgd_base
columns.definition: Loss given default under the base scenario — the share of exposure expected to be lost once a default happens, after recoveries and collateral. A RATIO: weight it by exposure, never average it.

columns.name: lgd_upturn
columns.definition: Loss given default under the upturn scenario.

columns.name: lgd_downturn
columns.definition: Loss given default under the downturn scenario. On a secured facility this is where a fall in collateral values shows up.

columns.name: ead_base_sar
columns.definition: Exposure at default under the base scenario: drawn balance plus the converted share of the undrawn limit. The exposure ECL is computed on, and the one an exposure-weighted average must weight by.

columns.name: ead_upturn_sar
columns.definition: Exposure at default under the upturn scenario.

columns.name: ead_downturn_sar
columns.definition: Exposure at default under the downturn scenario.

columns.name: ccf_base
columns.definition: Credit conversion factor under the base scenario — the share of the undrawn limit expected to be drawn before default. It is what makes exposure at default exceed today's balance on a card.

columns.name: ccf_upturn
columns.definition: Credit conversion factor under the upturn scenario.

columns.name: ccf_downturn
columns.definition: Credit conversion factor under the downturn scenario.

columns.name: scenario_weight_base
columns.definition: The probability weight on the base scenario. The three weights sum to one, which is the invariant a scenario-weight test checks.

columns.name: scenario_weight_upturn
columns.definition: The probability weight on the upturn scenario.

columns.name: scenario_weight_downturn
columns.definition: The probability weight on the downturn scenario.

columns.name: ecl_base_sar
columns.definition: Expected credit loss under the base scenario.

columns.name: ecl_upturn_sar
columns.definition: Expected credit loss under the upturn scenario.

columns.name: ecl_downturn_sar
columns.definition: Expected credit loss under the downturn scenario.

columns.name: ecl_weighted_sar
columns.definition: Probability-weighted ECL across the three scenarios.

columns.name: management_overlay_sar
columns.definition: Overlay applied on top of the modelled result. Kept separate and visible.

columns.name: ecl_final_sar
columns.definition: Weighted ECL plus overlay. The loss allowance carried for this facility.

columns.name: ecl_coverage_ratio
columns.definition: ecl_final_sar / gross_carrying_amount_sar. Null where the exposure is zero.
columns.aggregation: recompute from summed ECL over summed GCA; never average the ratio

columns.name: allowance_scope
columns.definition: What the loss allowance is measured on — the facility as a whole, here, rather than a portion of it.

columns.name: ecl_horizon_type
columns.definition: Which horizon this facility's ECL covers — twelve months for Stage 1, remaining lifetime for Stage 2, and the recovery profile for Stage 3. It is the sentence that explains why two facilities of the same size carry very different allowances.

columns.name: ecl_horizon_months
columns.definition: Months of DEFAULT EVENTS the calculation counts. Stage 1 counts twelve (or the shorter remaining life); it does not truncate the loss from those defaults at month twelve.

columns.name: ecl_expected_life_months
columns.definition: The life the lifetime ECL was computed over. On a revolving facility this is a behavioural estimate, not the contractual term.

columns.name: behavioural_expected_life_months
columns.definition: The expected remaining life the behavioural view assumes, which on a revolving facility is not the contractual term.

columns.name: recovery_rate_nominal
columns.definition: The share of exposure expected to be recovered, before discounting. One minus this, discounted for the delay, is LGD.

columns.name: recovery_delay_months
columns.definition: How long recoveries take to arrive. The delay is why a nominal recovery rate and a discounted one differ.

columns.name: expected_sale_cost_ratio
columns.definition: Costs of realising collateral, as a share of its value. It is why LGD on a fully secured facility is not zero.

columns.name: scenario_set_id
columns.definition: The forward-looking scenario set used.

columns.name: scenario_set_version
columns.definition: The version of that scenario set.

columns.name: pd_curve_id
columns.definition: The PD term structure applied to this facility.

columns.name: lgd_curve_id
columns.definition: The LGD curve applied to this facility.

columns.name: ead_curve_id
columns.definition: The EAD curve applied to this facility.

columns.name: recovery_cashflow_ref
columns.definition: The recovery cashflow profile used.

columns.name: discount_method
columns.definition: How the monthly discount rate was derived from the annual one, stated so the discounting can be reproduced.

columns.name: effective_annual_interest_rate
columns.definition: The annual rate including fees, on the same basis the customer is quoted. The rate the ECL discounting uses.

columns.name: calculation_method_label
columns.definition: The calculation method, in words — a transparent monthly-hazard expected credit loss in this installation.

columns.name: monitoring_as_of_date
columns.definition: The month-end this monitoring observation was taken at.

columns.name: prediction_reference_date
columns.definition: The date the prediction was made as at. Everything used to make it must be knowable on this date, which is what stops an outcome leaking into a predictor.

columns.name: score_target_definition_id
columns.definition: The outcome both scorecards are measured against, as a governed definition.

columns.name: performance_window_months
columns.definition: How long the performance window is — twelve months here.

columns.name: performance_window_start
columns.definition: The first month of the window this observation's outcome is measured over.

columns.name: performance_window_end
columns.definition: The last month of that window. Where it is in the future, the outcome is not yet knowable, and a default rate computed over this row is a rate over the defaults that have already happened.

columns.name: observed_followup_months
columns.definition: How many months of the window have actually elapsed. Below the window length the cohort is immature.

columns.name: outcome_known_at
columns.definition: The date the twelve-month outcome became knowable. Later than snapshot_date, always.

columns.name: performance_window_complete_flag
columns.definition: Whether all twelve follow-up months fall inside the published history.

columns.name: censoring_reason
columns.definition: Why an outcome is not observed for this row, in words. Usually that the window has not closed.

columns.name: observed_default_within_window
columns.definition: Whether a NEW default was observed in the twelve months after this snapshot. An EVALUATION label. It became knowable at `outcome_known_at` and must never be used as a predictor or shown as a current fact.
columns.null_policy: NULL where the window has not fully elapsed and no event was observed. An unobserved non-default is NOT a good.

columns.name: observed_30plus_within_window
columns.definition: Whether 30+ DPD was observed in the twelve months after. An EVALUATION label. It became knowable at `outcome_known_at` and must never be used as a predictor or shown as a current fact.
columns.null_policy: NULL where the window has not fully elapsed and no event was observed. An unobserved non-default is NOT a good.

columns.name: observed_60plus_within_window
columns.definition: Whether 60+ DPD was observed in the twelve months after. An EVALUATION label. It became knowable at `outcome_known_at` and must never be used as a predictor or shown as a current fact.
columns.null_policy: NULL where the window has not fully elapsed and no event was observed. An unobserved non-default is NOT a good.

columns.name: monitoring_eligible_flag
columns.definition: Whether this row belongs in a forward-default cohort: it is excluded if the facility was already in default at the prediction date.

columns.name: monitoring_exclusion_reason
columns.definition: Why a facility is not in the monitoring cohort — already in default at the observation date, most often. Excluding it is right, and it is why a default rate over this book is not a count of defaults over a count of rows.

columns.name: monitoring_reference_id
columns.definition: The key of the monthly monitoring cohort this row belongs to.

columns.name: monitoring_reference_type
columns.definition: How the monitoring cohort was formed — a monthly landmark cohort: everyone eligible at this month-end, followed forward.

columns.name: model_use_population
columns.definition: Whether this row is in the population a model may be measured on. A facility already in default is excluded from a PD test: its outcome is known before the prediction is made.

import_rules: Every column must be mapped explicitly; unmapped source columns are rejected.
Probabilities arrive as decimals in [0, 1]. A percentage is not converted by guessing.
Duplicate primary keys are rejected, never silently de-duplicated.
Supplied historical outcome labels are treated as restricted monitoring labels and excluded from operational prediction views.
Imported real data and synthetic rows are never mixed into one dataset version without separately labelled lineage.
Corporate entity types, rating grades and company financial statements are out of scope and are rejected with a retail-only message.
